drawings.description: devant « $\varepsilon \in \mathfrak{S}_0$ », un petit croquis de 0-sphère : deux courts traits verticaux, joints par deux traits légèrement courbes, l'un au-dessus de l'autre.
drawings.kind: 0-sphere sketch (two strokes joined by two lines)
drawings.notes: Two short vertical strokes (the two places of the 0-sphere), joined by two slightly curved lines, an upper and a lower one, which leave the left stroke at two computed points and meet on the right stroke at one computed point. Nothing struck. Disagreement in part with the note of the transcription (« deux points joints par un trait »): the two ends are short strokes and the join is doubled (an upper and a lower line), as the new \drawing mark says. Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128): to check again. Question settled by a machine pass on the facsimile, 2026-11-12 (page): the sketch is two short vertical strokes joined by two lines, an upper nearly straight one and a lower curved one, as drawn; the note's « deux points joints par un trait » describes it loosely. Not checked by a reader.

drawings.description: devant « $s \in S$ », le même croquis de 0-sphère : deux courts traits verticaux joints par deux traits, l'un au-dessus de l'autre.
drawings.kind: 0-sphere sketch (two strokes joined by two lines)
drawings.notes: The same sketch as on p. 3: two short vertical strokes; an upper line starting just left of the left stroke and rising to the right stroke; a lower line starting with a small hook under the middle and rising to the same computed point of the right stroke. Nothing struck. Disagreement in part with the note (« le même dessin de 0-sphère »): as on p. 3 the ends are strokes and the join is doubled; here the lower line does not reach the left stroke. Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128): to check again. Question settled by a machine pass on the facsimile, 2026-11-12 (page): the same sketch as on p. 3, two short vertical strokes joined by two lines, the lower one starting with a small hook short of the left stroke, as drawn. Not checked by a reader.

drawings.description: un segment horizontal : un point marqué $a$ à gauche, un trait passant par $b$ (petite marque verticale) et finissant en $c$ ; les lettres $a$, $b$, $c$ sous le segment.
drawings.notes: A full point a at the left, a horizontal line starting just right of it, a small vertical tick at b where the line passes, and the line ending at c with a short tick; the letters a, b, c under it. The small gap between the point a and the start of the line is on the page. Nothing struck. Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128): to check again.

drawings.description: en marge gauche, une bande oblique hachurée, coupée transversalement par quatre arcs épais marqués (de haut en bas) $y$, $b$, $a$, $x$ ; la partie entre $b$ et $a$ plus fortement hachurée, les arcs $a$ et $x$ partant d'un même point du bord gauche.
drawings.kind: hatched band cut by four arcs (a « faille »)
drawings.notes: A long oblique band (two straight sides, a faint cap at each end, the right side running a little past the lower cap as on the page), cut across by four thick arcs, all ending on the sides at computed points: y at the top, then b, then a; the arc x leaves the left side at the same computed point as a and curves down to the right side. The part between b and a is densely hatched (drawn as a hatched region); the light hatching elsewhere is drawn as a few pencil strokes at approximately their places, not stroke for stroke. Labels as on the page: y on both sides of its arc, b at the left and a glyph read b at the right of its arc, a at the left (above x) and at the right of its arc, x at the left and at the lower end of its arc. Doubtful: the glyph at the right of the second arc (read b, could be a), and the lower label of x. Nothing struck. Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128): to check again. Question settled by a machine pass on the facsimile, 2026-11-12 (maths): each arc carries its letter at both ends (y and y, a and a, x and x), so the glyph at the right end of the second arc is b and the lower label of the last arc is x, as drawn. Not checked by a reader. 2026-11-13, Claude Opus 5.5, overlay check (issue 147): not compiled (no TeX in the session); the TikZ rasterised and laid over the 350 dpi colour render of the scan, with ink/pencil separations of the crop. Redrawn on the ink: the sides of the band as the slightly bent lines they are; the top of the band is not a cap joining the sides but the first of the hatching strokes (it touches neither side), and the lower end is closed by a pencil stroke from the left corner only, running on past the right side's line; the four arcs through points read on them (b was 1.5 units low); the hatching stroke for stroke instead of a pattern and a few strokes at approximate places: above b, eight strokes (five in ink, three in pencil), between b and a the eleven heavy strokes of the dense hatching, below a and x six faint pencil strokes, two of them broken; the eight labels on their glyphs. Every element lies on the ink to within about 1 unit.
